collections.title: The Lord of the Rings — cover sets
collections.intro: Most readers met The Lord of the Rings in three volumes, and each edition dressed the three books in one design. Each set here is one edition: from the Allen & Unwin jackets Tolkien designed in 1954 and Barbara Remington's Ballantine paperbacks of 1965 to Pauline Baynes, Darrell K. Sweet, John Howe and Alan Lee, the film and television tie-ins, and editions in French, German, Spanish, Dutch, Chinese and Indonesian. A set appears only where Open Library holds a front cover of the same design for each volume; editions that reuse another edition's artwork are left out.

collections.title: The Great American Novel
collections.intro: The Great American Novel is the old idea of one book that would catch the whole of the United States — its promise, its violence, its many voices. The phrase is from John William De Forest in 1868, and critics have argued ever since about which book, if any, comes closest. These are novels the Wikipedia article on the idea discusses as candidates, from The Last of the Mohicans to Underworld, each with one cover chosen by hand — the first edition's where Open Library holds a clean one.

collections.title: Rowohlts Monographien
collections.intro: From 1958 Rowohlt published small paperback lives, each of one person told in their own words and in pictures — writers, composers, painters, philosophers, politicians. The classic cover is a portrait photograph tinted in one colour across the whole front, the name in a bar at the top and the little rororo box at the bottom. One book per person, in series order, from the covers Open Library has in that design.

collections.title: Heyne Bibliothek der Science Fiction Literatur
collections.intro: Heyne's „Bibliothek der Science Fiction Literatur“, edited by Wolfgang Jeschke from 1981 to 2001: about a hundred classics of the genre in the „white series“ — a white cover, the series header at the top and one square colour picture. Shown in series order, from the covers Open Library has in that design.

collections.title: Folio — Gallimard
collections.intro: Folio is Gallimard's numbered paperback series, launched in 1972; number 1 was Malraux's La Condition humaine, number 2 Camus's L'Étranger. Robert Massin gave it a white cover with author and title in black Baskerville above a single picture, a design that stayed in use until the end of 2010. Volumes from the first few hundred numbers in that design, one per author, in number order, from the covers Open Library has.

collections.title: Présence du futur — Denoël
collections.intro: Présence du futur was the science-fiction series of the Paris publisher Denoël, founded in 1954 by Robert Kanters and published until 2000. From 1975 its covers were illustrated, at first with the picture inside a central circle on a colour gradient, until the art spread over the whole page towards the end of the 1980s. This wall shows the circle design only — first printings of the late 1970s and early 1980s and reprints of older numbers — one per work, in number order, from the covers Open Library has.

collections.title: Spektrum — Volk und Welt
collections.intro: Spektrum was a paperback series from Verlag Volk und Welt in East Berlin, 1968 to 1993, 279 titles, mostly stories and short novels by foreign authors. Its black jacket — author and title in white at the top, the word „Spektrum“ at the right and one black-grey-white image below, nearly all by Lothar Reher — gave it its nickname, the „black series“. Only the volumes Open Library holds pictures of.

collections.title: Virago Modern Classics
collections.intro: Virago launched its Modern Classics in 1978 with Antonia White's Frost in May, reissuing out-of-print books by women writers. For years the paperbacks shared one design: a dark green band carrying the author and title, above a painting chosen for the book, often a detail. The back covers name the picture. This wall gathers the green-band printings Open Library holds covers for, and gives the painting where a scan of the same printing, or a collector quoting her own copy, names it.

collections.intro: In 1966–68 Heinz Edelmann drew a run of covers for the Fischer Bücherei that Sammlung Keller calls style-defining for the series layout: a coloured band with the fish logo, the author and title set in black, and below them a full picture in his flat, bright colours of those years, a year or two before Yellow Submarine. These are the ten Sammlung Keller shows.

collections.title: Penguin Classics — the black-band years
collections.intro: From the mid-1980s into the early 2000s, Penguin Classics wore a cream frame, a black panel for author and title, and a period picture chosen for each book. The back cover named the picture, often down to the gallery that lent it: Caspar David Friedrich's Moonrise on the Seashore for The Moonstone, Caillebotte for The Ambassadors, a Greek vase for Pindar. Where a scan of the same printing on the Internet Archive names the picture, the credit is shown as printed; the rest are left blank rather than guessed.

collections.title: Fischer Bücherei
collections.intro: The Fischer Bücherei was S. Fischer's paperback series from 1952 to about 1970: over a thousand numbered volumes, a different picture on every cover. The first covers ran a picture over the whole front with the series name at the foot; from about 1962 a coloured band with the three fish sits at the top above a white title field. This wall shows the volumes whose series cover Open Library holds, in the order of their numbers, and names the designer where it is known for that printing.

collections.title: Steinbeck at dtv — covers by Celestino Piatti
collections.intro: From the mid-1980s dtv reissued John Steinbeck's books in German with covers by the Swiss artist Celestino Piatti: one bold black line drawing on a single colour for each book, signed in the corner. These are the covers Sammlung Keller shows, in the order of their dtv numbers.

collections.title: Herder Bücherei — covers by Walter Grieder
collections.intro: The Swiss illustrator Walter Grieder drew covers for the Herder Bücherei, Herder's paperback series, from the late 1950s into the early 1970s: first bright, crowded pictures across the whole front, later a single bold motif in a white frame. These are the covers Sammlung Keller shows, in the order of their numbers.

collections.title: Haffmans — covers by Nikolaus Heidelbach
collections.intro: From the late 1980s the Zurich publisher Haffmans dressed its crime novels and much of its fiction in covers by Nikolaus Heidelbach: one strange, exactly painted object on black — a lipstick with a nail through it, a cigar, a swan with a red hood in its beak. These are the covers Sammlung Keller shows; Keller gives no titles, so they were read from the covers themselves.

collections.title: Kipling at Haffmans — covers by Nikolaus Heidelbach
collections.intro: Haffmans published a German Kipling edition in the late 1980s and 1990s, and Nikolaus Heidelbach drew a black-and-white picture for the panel on each volume: a tiger, a panther, an elephant, three schoolboys. Kim is shown in the Büchergilde Gutenberg edition, which kept the design. These are the volumes Sammlung Keller shows.

collections.title: Ex Libris — covers by Hanspeter Wyss
collections.intro: From 1961 into the early 1980s the Swiss illustrator Hanspeter Wyss drew dust jackets for Ex Libris, the Zurich book club, and for Benziger: flat bright shapes, a crowd of houses, a skyline of crystals, a harlequin under an umbrella. Ex Libris kept no numbered series, so these follow Sammlung Keller's dates roughly, with the undated ones last. Some carry only type and an abstract figure, such as a target, a colour wheel or a grid.
